items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The helper name `_filter_prefetch_queryset` says what it does, the variables (`predicate`, `low_mark`, `high_mark`, `window`) are clear, and formatting matches Django style. It has no docstring, but the reference solution has none either. Minor gap only.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One short private helper (~20 lines) is shared by the reverse-FK and M2M paths. It reuses ORM building blocks (Window, RowNumber, GreaterThan/LessThanOrEqual, clear_limits, get_order_by) and leaves the QuerySet.filter guard alone. No dead code, and the temporary test was removed.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Checks `features.supports_over_clause` and raises a specific NotSupportedError with a clear message. Calls `queryset._clone()` before `clear_limits()` so the caller's queryset isn't changed. Handles high_mark None. No magic constants.

items.name: Per-parent slice semantics for open/bounded slices
items.name_zh: 开放/有界切片按父对象分区
items.evidence: Builds `Window(RowNumber(), partition_by=field_name, order_by=order_by)` with `GreaterThan(window, low_mark)` and adds LessThanOrEqual only `if high_mark is not None`. It calls `clear_limits()` on a clone (`queryset._clone()`), so the slice is applied per parent in SQL and the user's queryset is untouched.
